messages.author: 839dfa09184985a5
messages.subject: Implementing CDF for SkewNormal
parts:
In order to implement the test for the cdf of Skew Normal, I need to define a var/fvar for the Owens_t function, T(h,a)--if I don't and try to use boost::math::owens_t, I get a seg fault. I can compute the partial with respect to a, but can't find a viable method for computing the partial with respect to h. Any ideas?

Also, are there any other distributions that need to be implemented other than Gumbel, Exp_Normal, and Skew_Normal?


Thanks,
Peter

parts:
I implemented owenst in special_functions in both stan::math and stan::agrad--I tested both, including the derivs--, but when I run the following in skew_normal_cdf_test

template <typename T_y, typename T_loc, typename T_scale,
typename T_shape, typename T4, typename T5,
typename T6, typename T7, typename T8,
typename T9>
typename stan::return_type<T_y, T_loc, T_scale,T_shape>::type
cdf_function(const T_y& y, const T_loc& mu, const T_scale& sigma,
const T_shape& alpha, const T4&, const T5&, const T6&, const T7&, const T8&, const T9&) {
return 0.5 * erfc(-(y - mu) / (sqrt(2) * sigma)) - 2.0 * stan::math::owenst((y - mu) / sigma, alpha);
}

I get a seg fault 11 (it comes from calling stan::math::owenst).

If I try using stan::agrad::owenst instead, I get "call of overloaded ‘owenst(double, const double&)’ is ambiguous".

Did I miss something in implementing owenst?


Thanks,
Peter

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Implementing CDF for SkewNormal
parts:
I'm not seeing the definition of owenst on the
fvar branch I just pulled from origin.

But what you probably want to do is follow the rest
of our implementations and write this as:

{
using stan::math::owenst;
return 0.5 * erfc(-(y - mu) / (sqrt(2) * sigma)) - 2.0 * owenst((y - mu) / sigma, alpha);
}

This will apply stan::math::owenst() if the argument is
a double because owenst is brought into the local namespace.

If the argument is stan::agrad::var, then it'll use
argument-dependent lookup to find the implementation in
the stan::agrad namespace. Ditto for fvar if you've gotten
around to doing that one, too.

Argument dependent lookup seems mysterious, but it was
designed for exactly this kind of overload:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argument-dependent_name_lookup

I'm about to add some refactoring that should make defining
new functions for agrad and fvar easier.

Also, make sure you have all three signatures defined in
agrad:

var owenst(double,var);
var owenst(var,double);
var owenst(var,var);

(I've never even heard of the Owens T function!)

- Bob
